Economic and social development in Asia and the Pacific
**NDB:** established in 2015 by BRICS countries; headquarters: Shanghai, China.
**Founding members:** Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa.
**In the 18th BRICS Summit 2026:** NDB President Dilma Rousseff attended as an important guest; NDB represents the BRICS-led development-finance institution.

parts.t: G20 and the Johannesburg Summit 2025
items: 19 countries plus European Union and African Union
**Venue and dates:** Johannesburg, South Africa; 22–23 November 2025.
The 20th G20 Summit at Johannesburg was the **first G20 Summit held on African soil**.
**Outcome:** leaders adopted the Johannesburg Leaders' Declaration; it reflected the African philosophy of Ubuntu – shared humanity.
**Key areas:** debt relief, climate finance, food security, energy transition and multilateral reforms.
**Mission 300:** supported at the Johannesburg G20 Summit; target: electricity access for 300 million Africans by 2030.

**Held:** 6–8 May 2026; venue: Lapu-Lapu City, Cebu, Philippines.

parts.t: SCO: the 26th Summit and the Heads of Government meeting
items: **Venue and dates:** Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan; 31 August–1 September 2026.
**Counter-terrorism:** India opposed double standards in counter-terrorism.
**Approach:** emphasised dialogue and diplomacy; linked Eurasian security with peace in Afghanistan.
**Connectivity:** supported connectivity that promotes trade while respecting sovereignty and territorial integrity.
**Language:** supported English as an official SCO language alongside Russian and Chinese.
**Forum:** announced the first SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum, to be hosted later in 2026.
SCO Council of Heads of Government
**India:** the Indian delegation was led by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh.

parts.t: BIMSTEC and the first Home Ministers' Meeting
items: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation
Seven countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand
**Held:** in New Delhi on 13 October 2026; chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
**Participation:** all seven member countries participated; the meeting adopted the Delhi Declaration.
**Background:** the ministerial mechanism was proposed at the 4th BIMSTEC Summit in Kathmandu, 2018, and welcomed at the 6th Summit in Bangkok, 2025.
**Cooperation against:** terrorism, organised crime, drug trafficking, human trafficking, cybercrime, money laundering and terror financing.
**Emphasised:** UNSC Resolution 1267 sanctions, intelligence sharing, extradition, mutual legal assistance and victim-centred protection.

parts.t: QUAD, G7, the One Health Summit and IBSA
items: **Members:** India, United States, Japan and Australia.
**Origins:** cooperation during the December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami relief operations.
**11th Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting:** held in New Delhi on 26 May 2026; hosted by India; External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar participated.
**Members:** Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, United Kingdom and United States; the European Union participates.
**52nd G7 Summit 2026:** venue Évian-les-Bains, France; dates 15–17 June 2026; French Presidency.
**Outreach:** invited outreach nations included India and Brazil.
**India at the G7:** India participated for the 13th time; PM Narendra Modi attended for the seventh consecutive time.
**Joint declarations adopted on:** public health and technology; migration and crime; economy and supply chains.
**Next:** the 53rd G7 Summit is scheduled in the United States in 2027.
**Held:** in Lyon, France, 5–7 April 2026, under the French G7 Presidency.
**One Health approach:** links human, animal, plant and ecosystem health.
**Supported by the Quadripartite:** WHO, FAO, UNEP and WOAH.
IBSA – India, Brazil and South Africa Dialogue Forum
**IBSA:** established in 2003; trilateral cooperation among India, Brazil and South Africa.
**At the 2025 G20 Johannesburg Summit:** India proposed digital cooperation and climate-resilient agriculture through IBSA dialogue.

parts.t: European Union and the 16th India–EU Summit

**Participants:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi; European Council President António Costa; European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.
**Major outcomes:** conclusion of India–EU Free Trade Agreement negotiations; first India–EU Security and Defence Partnership; “Towards 2030” Strategic Agenda.

parts.t: UNFCCC, COP30 and COP31
items: UNFCCC – United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
**Belém 4x Pledge:** quadruple sustainable fuel use by 2035 compared with 2024; includes green hydrogen, advanced biofuels and e-fuels.
**Support and tracking:** 23 countries endorsed the Belém 4x Pledge; IEA to track progress.
**Other COP30 initiatives:** Belém Action Mechanism; Belém Health Action Plan; Climate Finance Work Programme; Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative.
**COP31:** scheduled for 9–20 November 2026; venue: Antalya, Türkiye.

parts.t: Environmental conventions: CBD, CMS, Ramsar, Montreal Protocol
items: **CBD:** adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit; Secretariat: Montreal, Canada.
**Objectives:** 1. conservation of biological diversity; 2. sustainable use of its components; 3. fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources.
**CMS:** also called the Bonn Convention; adopted in 1979; Secretariat: Bonn, Germany.
**Focus:** conservation of migratory species and their habitats.
**Ramsar Convention:** adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran; focus: conservation and wise use of wetlands.

**India's Ramsar sites:** India reported 101 Ramsar sites in the relevant passage; the addition of Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Uttar Pradesh) on 15 October 2026 raised the total to 103.
**Tamil Nadu:** listed as the State with the highest number of Ramsar sites.
**Adopted:** 1987; focus: protection of the ozone layer through phase-out of ozone-depleting substances.
**Kigali Amendment:** adopted on 15 October 2016 in Rwanda; focuses on the phase-down of HFCs.

lectures.title: Science and technology: space, AI, supercomputing and semiconductors

parts.t: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission
items: **Objective:** study Mars' two moons, Phobos and Deimos, and return samples to Earth.
**Intended sample:** at least 10 grams from Phobos.
**Timeline:** planned mission duration approximately five years; expected arrival at Mars: 2027; expected sample return to Earth: 2031.
**Scientific objective:** determine whether the moons are captured asteroids or debris from a giant impact on Mars.
**Wider value:** the mission may improve understanding of planetary formation and the delivery of water and organic compounds.
Quasi-satellite orbit around Mars near Phobos
Measures surface distance using laser pulses
NASA instrument measuring gamma rays and neutrons
IDEFIX, developed jointly by France's CNES and Germany's DLR
**NASA's part:** NASA's MEGANE instrument is part of the mission; NASA's Deep Space Network supports communication and navigation.
**Sample share:** NASA is expected to receive approximately 15% of the returned samples for research and curation.
**Samplers:** JAXA's C-Sampler collects subsurface material; NASA's P-Sampler uses high-pressure nitrogen gas to collect surface particles.

parts.t: GAGAN and India's first satellite-based landing by a commercial jet
items: India demonstrated its **first Satellite-Based Landing System (SLS) approach by a commercial jet** using indigenous GAGAN.
**How:** the aircraft used satellite-derived guidance instead of relying on a conventional Instrument Landing System (ILS).
GAGAN – GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation
**Developed by:** ISRO and the Airports Authority of India (AAI).
**What it does:** enhances GPS accuracy; provides integrity information for safer aircraft navigation; supports satellite-based landing and other applications beyond aviation.
Monitor GPS signals and detect errors
Calculate signal corrections and integrity information
Connect GAGAN stations and transmit data
**GAGAN:** enhances GPS signals for precise aircraft navigation and landing.
**NavIC:** India's indigenous regional navigation satellite system, providing positioning, navigation and timing services.

parts.t: SOLAR-1: the US space-weather satellite
items: **Name:** SOLAR-1 stands for Space Weather Observations at L1 to Advance Readiness–1; previously called Space Weather Follow On–Lagrange 1 (SWFO-L1).
**SOLAR-1** is described as the first US satellite designed exclusively for continuous operational space-weather observations.
**Launch:** launched on 24 September 2025; launch vehicle: SpaceX Falcon 9; launch site: Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
**Journey:** reached its intended orbit after approximately four months; final engine burn: 23 January 2026.
**Data:** operated by NOAA; data transmitted to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) for forecasts, watches, warnings and alerts.
**Significance:** space-weather monitoring helps predict solar events that may affect satellites, communications, navigation systems, power infrastructure and space missions.

parts.t: Chandrayaan-3: the Vikram lander hop experiment
items: **The hop:** Vikram lander reignited its engines and performed a controlled hop on the Moon; it landed approximately 50 cm away from its original position.
**Purpose:** the experiment primarily tested ascent capabilities relevant to future sample-return missions.
**ChaSTE:** Chandra's Surface Thermophysical Experiment, a lunar thermometer, was re-penetrated into the lunar regolith at the new location.
A distinct two-layer structure was identified in the top 6.5 cm of the post-hop site
Soil cohesion and density increased with depth
Local craters and depressions caused temperatures to fall faster than global models predicted
Engine firing blew away the top 3 cm of regolith and slightly compacted the underlying material

parts.t: NASA's Artemis II mission
items: **Artemis II** was a crewed lunar flyby mission, not a Moon-landing mission; it was the first crewed Artemis flight.
**Flight:** lifted off from Kennedy Space Center; the crew completed a lunar flyby and returned to Earth.
**Tested:** the Space Launch System (SLS), Orion spacecraft, ground systems, recovery teams and mission procedures.
**Milestone:** the mission marked the return of humans to the vicinity of the Moon after the Apollo era.
**Operations:** test communications, control and navigation; test manual operation in deep space.
**Crew:** evaluate crew living and working conditions.
**Future:** validate systems needed for future lunar surface operations and crewed Mars missions.
**Artemis I problem:** Artemis I had shown unexpected cracking and shedding of Avcoat heat-shield material.
**Cause:** NASA attributed this to heat and gases accumulating inside the material, producing internal pressure and uneven shedding.
**Artemis II result:** re-entry was closely monitored; NASA's initial inspection found that the heat shield performed as expected, with significantly reduced char loss compared with Artemis I.
**Artemis III:** 2027 low-Earth-orbit demonstration to test one or both commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin.

parts.t: Pixxel: the orbital data-centre satellite and the EO constellation
items: India's first orbital data-centre satellite – Pathfinder
**Partnership:** Pixxel announced a strategic partnership with Sarvam to develop India's first orbital data-centre satellite.
**Demonstrator:** the satellite is a single-satellite demonstrator.
Design, build, launch and operate Pathfinder; provide hyperspectral imaging payload
Provide sovereign AI models and inference infrastructure: the AI backbone for language models, training and inference directly in orbit
Pixxel's planned satellite-production facility, designed to scale production to up to 100 units
What is an orbital data centre?
**Definition:** a space-based computing system in which satellites carry high-performance processors, such as data-centre-class GPUs.
**AI in orbit:** AI models can run directly in orbit rather than relying entirely on ground-based data centres.
**Edge computing:** processing data closer to where it is generated is similar to edge computing.
**Aim:** to reduce the need to transmit large volumes of raw satellite data to Earth.
India's first commercial Earth Observation satellite constellation
**Agreement:** on 21 January 2026, IN-SPACe formalised an agreement with a Pixxel-led consortium called Allied Orbits.
**Objective:** establish India's first indigenous commercial Earth Observation (EO) satellite constellation under the Earth Observation Public-Private Partnership (EO-PPP) programme.
**Consortium members:** Pixxel Space India; Piersight Space; SatSure Analytics India; Dhruva Space.
**Plan:** investment of more than ₹1,200 crore over five years from January 2026; constellation of 12 Earth Observation satellites; operationalisation by 2029.
**Sensors:** panchromatic, multispectral, hyperspectral and microwave Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR).
**Applications:** climate monitoring, disaster management, agriculture, infrastructure planning and geospatial services.
**EO-PPP objective:** build a national Earth Observation data backbone, reduce dependence on foreign satellite data and strengthen India's private-sector space ecosystem.

parts.t: New telescopes in Ladakh and the COSMOS-2 Planetarium
items: **Union Budget 2026–27:** announced four astronomy infrastructure projects.
2-metre-class ground-based telescope; observes the Sun in optical and near-infrared wavelengths; studies the origin and behaviour of solar magnetic fields
Segmented primary mirror: 13.7 metres; adaptive optics for sharper infrared imaging; spectrographs and imagers
Existing 2-metre optical-infrared telescope; planned upgrade: 3.7-metre segmented telescope
Implementing institution: Indian Institute of Astrophysics
**HCT history:** first light: 26 September 2000; regular observations began: May 2003.
**HCT operation:** remote operation from CREST near Bengaluru through a satellite link.

parts.t: ISRO's LVM3-M6 and BlueBird Block-2; other space developments
items: **Result:** ISRO/NSIL successfully placed the BlueBird Block-2 communications satellite into its intended orbit.
**BlueBird Block-2**, payload mass 6,100 kg, is the heaviest payload launched by LVM3 from Indian soil.
**Counts:** the 104th launch from Sriharikota; ninth successful LVM3 mission; third dedicated commercial mission; 100% reliability for the launch vehicle at that stage.
**BlueBird Block-2 features:** phased-array antenna area 223 m²; described as the largest commercial communications satellite deployed into LEO.
**Purpose:** part of a global satellite constellation designed to provide direct-to-smartphone connectivity; intended to support 4G and 5G voice/video calls, texts, streaming and data services.
**MOI-1A:** India's first orbital computing satellite; developed by startup TakeMe2Space; launched/referenced on 2 October 2026; designed for AI-based data processing in space.
**Vikram-1:** developed by Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace; described as India's first privately developed orbital launch vehicle.
**Mission Aagaman:** Vikram-1 made a successful flight under Mission Aagaman on 18 July 2026 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
**Haven-1:** private commercial space station being developed by Vast; described as the world's first commercial privately operated space station.
**SMILE mission:** joint project of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and European Space Agency (ESA); full form: Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer.
**MAVEN mission:** NASA's Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN mission.
**Alaknanda:** spiral galaxy discovered by Indian astronomers.
**Sputnik-1:** first artificial satellite, launched on 4 October 1957; highlighted in connection with World Space Week.
**National Space Day 2026:** 23 August; theme “Towards Viksit Bharat: Innovating, Collaborating and Aspiring to Global Space Leadership.” Main ceremony: Ahmedabad.

parts.t: India AI Impact Summit 2026
items: **Dates and venue:** 16–21 February 2026; Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
The India AI Impact Summit 2026 was the **first AI Impact Summit hosted by a Global South nation**.
AI reflecting languages, cultures and identities
Equitable access to data, computing, models and infrastructure
**AI for Economic Development and Social Good**
**Global AI Impact Commons:** launched at the summit; more than 80 impact stories; contributions from over 30 countries; designed to share practical AI applications and experiences.
**AI infrastructure:** India had a target of 10,000 GPUs and had reached 38,000 GPUs at the time of the summit section; target of 570 Data Labs across the country.
**SAHI and BODH – Health AI:** launched on 17 February 2026 at the India AI Impact Summit.
**SAHI:** Strategy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare for India; a national guidance framework for responsible AI adoption in healthcare.

**SAHI's direction:** provides direction on governance, data stewardship, validation, deployment and monitoring; encourages coordination among health institutions, technology developers, researchers and policymakers.
**BODH:** Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI; developed by IIT Kanpur with the National Health Authority.
**BODH's working:** a privacy-preserving benchmarking platform; evaluates AI models using diverse, anonymised real-world health data; allows evaluation without sharing underlying datasets.
**AI-Preneurs of India:** launched by Atal Innovation Mission under NITI Aayog at the India AI Impact Summit on 17 February 2026.
**The book:** a coffee-table book documenting the journeys of 45 AI startups; focuses on startups applying AI to real-world problems.
**AIKosh – IndiaAI Mission:** IndiaAI Mission approved in March 2024; AIKosh is a key pillar and unified national data platform.

parts.t: AI in education, skilling, cybersecurity and governance
items: India's first dedicated Quantum and AI University Campus
**MoU:** signed on 20 February 2026 between the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), under MeitY, and the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
**Location:** Amaravati Quantum Valley; described as India's first dedicated Quantum and AI university campus.
**Intended to combine:** quantum science; artificial intelligence; deep-tech talent development; industry-aligned skilling.
Bodhan AI Centre of Excellence and Bharat EduAI Stack
**Event:** Bharat Bodhan AI Conclave 2026; 12–13 February 2026; Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; launch by Dharmendra Pradhan.
**Bodhan AI Centre of Excellence:** formally launched; IIT Madras chosen as institutional anchor; established as the IIT Madras Bodhan AI Foundation.
**Bodhan AI:** an IIT Madras-incubated initiative supported by the Ministry of Education; intended to build sovereign AI digital public infrastructure for education.
**Bharat EduAI Stack:** introduced as an open, interoperable architecture for AI in education.
**Bharat EduAI Stack applications:** personalised AI tutors; AI-assisted teacher training; institutional administration; data-driven policy-making; use of large learning datasets.
**Organised by:** Department of Telecommunications at India Mobile Congress 2026; date: 10 October 2026.
**Theme:** “Creating Innovative Agents in 5G.” Inaugurated by Dr Bilel Jamoussi of ITU.
**First prize:** Team Netaxis, RVCE Bengaluru; project: “Context Aware Agentic Orchestration of QoS and Adaptive Security in Resource Constrained 5G.”
**Launched:** 15 August 2026; organisation: NIELIT; a national cybersecurity and AI hackathon.
**Design:** to test human judgement in cybersecurity assessment rather than only speed of vulnerability detection.
**Partners:** collaboration: Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC Foundation); knowledge partner: CERT-In.
**Final round:** named “The Kesari”, scheduled for November 2026 at Dr Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi; ten finalist teams.
**Titles:** winner's title: Cyber Kesari 2026; runners-up titles: Rustam and Pahalwan.
**First UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance:** Geneva, 6–7 July 2026; India represented by Minister of State Kirti Vardhan Singh.
**Purpose:** intended as a universal, multi-stakeholder platform for international AI governance; seeks to complement, not replace, existing national, regional and international initiatives.

**Major concerns:** deepfakes and AI-generated disinformation; influence on elections and public trust; large AI systems' electricity and water consumption; need for international coordination and safeguards.

parts.t: Supercomputing: LineShine, the TOP500 and PARAM Pragya
items: LineShine – world's fastest supercomputer in the June 2026 TOP500
**Rank:** ranked first in the 67th edition of the TOP500 list; displaced El Capitan of the United States.
**LineShine** is the first TOP500 system to exceed two exaflops of sustained double-precision performance using CPUs only.
Top five exascale systems in the June 2026 TOP500
National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting
**Inaugurated:** 8 August 2026, remotely by Prime Minister Narendra Modi; location: IIT Delhi's Sonipat campus, Haryana.
**Facility:** an AI-oriented high-performance computing facility, installed with 400 NVIDIA A100 GPUs; each GPU has 80 GB memory; computing capacity: 250 AI petaflops.
**Funding:** announced funding of ₹120 crore from the Government through DST and MeitY.
**Research areas:** large-scale AI models; materials discovery; energy; healthcare; robotics.
**NSM:** listed in DST Annual Report 2025–26 among recent deployments under the National Supercomputing Mission.

parts.t: Semiconductors: DHRUV64 and chip projects
items: **DHRUV64:** indigenous technology; launched: 15 December 2025; developer: C-DAC.
**DHRUV64** is India's first indigenous 64-bit dual-core microprocessor, developed by the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC).
**Importance:** highlighted as an important development in indigenous processor design and domestic semiconductor capability.
India Semiconductor Mission – two additional projects
**Approval:** two additional semiconductor projects approved on 5 May 2026; projects located in Gujarat.
**Numbers:** combined investment approximately ₹3,936 crore; expected skilled employment: 2,230 jobs.
**Context:** part of India's efforts to develop a domestic semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.
India's first chip fabrication plant at a commercial SEZ, Dholera
**Description:** described as India's first chip fabrication plant at a commercial SEZ; an AI-enabled semiconductor fabrication facility.
**Intended to support:** electronics hardware, software and IT/ITES services.
India's first advanced 3D semiconductor packaging unit
**Event:** foundation stone laid for India's first advanced 3D chip-packaging unit.
**Nature:** a greenfield, vertically integrated advanced packaging and embedded glass-substrate ATMP facility; it is not a conventional semiconductor fabrication plant.
**Programme:** part of the semiconductor plants approved under India's semiconductor programme.
**Odisha:** described as the first State to host both India's first compound semiconductor fabrication unit and an advanced 3D chip-packaging facility based on glass substrates.

parts.t: Semiconductor Mission 2.0 and electronics manufacturing schemes
items: **Intended to strengthen:** semiconductor equipment and materials; full-stack intellectual property; domestic manufacturing; supply-chain resilience.
**Budget allocation:** an allocation of ₹20,000 crore over five years in the Budget context.
**Semicon 2.0 approval:** it also refers to a separate Semicon 2.0 approval with an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore and six pillars.
**Targets mentioned:** 200 design startups and one lakh technicians over five years.
**ECMS:** notified on 8 April 2025; initial outlay: ₹22,919 crore; increased to ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026–27.
**Supports:** domestic manufacturing of electronic components and supply-chain development.
**Progress:** 106 approved projects across 15 States, with expected investment of ₹69,548 crore.
